title: improv·artist · sound (Janet Cardiff)
mutation_directive: improv artist: sound via Janet Cardiff

improv_extras.practice: binaural sound walks; 40-part motet; spatial audio as place

v1.feedback: The 40-voice interference pattern on a parabolic bowl is a legit translation of Cardiff's motet spatiality into particle form, but the result reads as a flat vibrating disk — the bowl curvature is too subtle at default camera to register as architectural volume. Tilt the camera to a lower angle (eye-level with the rim) so the parabolic depth and wave displacement read as a 3D resonance chamber, not a pond surface. The palette is tastefully restrained but the interference pattern is too uniform — consider making a handful of voices significantly louder (Cardiff's soloists) so constructive nodes form visible bright loci rather than even shimmer. The form needs to fill more vertical screen real estate; right now it's a horizontal slab floating in dark void.

v2.feedback: The 40-voice circular interference maps Cardiff's motet layout faithfully, but the visual result is a rippling parabolic bowl — more physics demo than felt experience of inhabiting polyphonic sound. To push this: let constructive-interference nodes spawn vertical filaments or standing-wave columns that rise from the surface (biomorphic, vascular), giving the piece a recognizable upward silhouette instead of a concave dish. The amber/silver palette is restrained and apt, but the wave displacement is too uniform and subtle — exaggerate the soloist loci into bright sculptural peaks so the 'hot spots' of interference become the subject, readable in 2 seconds as a sonic landscape rather than a textured surface.
